commit.message: Add end-to-end macOS installer with hardware-aware model calibration and verified deployment
Port Strata v0.1.13 to Apple Silicon with validated GGUF Metal backend

prompt path: never write into the borrowable cache slots while laying out (a resident expert was corrupted)

When serving, the prompt path lays its buffers out at start in the expert-cache slots it may borrow, but those
slots hold resident experts until a request lends them. Writing the MMQ row table at layout time overwrote part
of a resident expert: decode later computed it on the GPU, and the first window that routed to it turned every
logit into NaN ("!!!!" from mid-answer, e.g. at position 138 of an 86-token prompt, even with the prompt read
through the windows). The table is written at the start of every prompt read, while the slots are lent.
STRATA_DBG_NAN=1 also reports the first verify window with non-finite logits and the state a prompt leaves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0154bwiad8gY7wRehCXy27pN

prompt path: zero the tail after the last gathered expert before MMQ (garbage answers after the first request)

MMQ reads up to one 256-value tile past a matrix's last row when the row is not a multiple of it (the down
product: 640 values). Those weights meet zero activations, harmless only if they decode finite; llama.cpp
zero-pads after every tensor. The group buffers held leftovers - after the first request's refill, other
experts' bytes read as IQ4_NL blocks - and a non-finite scale times zero gave NaN logits ("!!!!" answers from
the second request on). The group buffers get a 4 KB tail, zeroed after the last expert before each launch.
The MMQ row table (in the lent slots the refill overwrites) is written at every prompt.
STRATA_DBG_NAN=1 reports the first layer of a chunk whose MoE produced non-finite values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0154bwiad8gY7wRehCXy27pN

engine 0.1.13: about 2x faster long prompts; stall reports for issue #31

Prompt path (bench/results/2026-09-28-prefill-speed):
- `--prefill auto`: chunks up to 8192 tokens, sized to the cache slots the prompt path may borrow; a
  request borrows only what its prompt needs (Prefill::relayout). setup writes it and switches old
  `--prefill 2048` configs once the engine supports it.
- The attention and MoE halves share one scratch region (~260 KB less per token).
- Experts through llama.cpp's MMQ kernels (ggml-cuda mmq.cuh, compiled from the same checkout as ggml
  into strata_mmq; Strata Q2_0 blobs converted to GGUF blocks on the gather; IQ1_M layers keep FP16).
- Chunks >= 2048: every non-resident expert streams through a ring in a fixed order across layers, so
  the next layer's arrive during its attention half (384 slots when the arena is pinned, else 96).
- The PLE block for the whole chunk at once; the next chunk's PLE rows read on a thread; unpinned
  experts copied by stager threads (epoch-tagged claims).
- STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1 prints a per-phase GPU timeline.
Q2_0 32K prompt 572 -> 1290 tok/s, IQ3_S 383 -> 1208 (RTX 5070 12 GB). Needles 5/5 1K-262K.

Issue #31 / #29: the serve watchdog (now 60 s) prints a stall report - each expert-pool thread's state,
the verify window's flags, layers served during the stall, memory and page faults - and on Windows
writes a minidump with every thread's stack; Release builds keep a PDB. The engine prints its version.

setup: recompile a locally built engine when its source changed (git pull on Linux, issue #31)

A compiled engine was stamped only as source=local, so later runs never rebuilt it and a
git pull kept the old binary (on Linux, where there is no ready-made engine, that also meant
no v0.1.12 pool fix). BUILD.json now keeps a hash of the engine's and the image encoder's
source files; on start a changed hash recompiles (incrementally, in build/) before the model
starts, and a failed compile falls back to the installed engine.

web app: attach text files - drop them on the chat or use the attach button (issue #30)

Text files (code, notes, logs, data; up to 512 KB) become chips next to
the message and are sent as "File: name" plus a fenced block (a longer
fence when the file contains one). Binary files are refused with a toast;
pictures work as before (when images are on). The attach button is always
there now. Kept small on purpose: the web app is for quick tests and
settings.

engine: fix a race in the CPU expert pool, and never hang silently again (issue #29, engine 0.1.12)

On a card with most experts in VRAM (RTX 4090) generation could stop for
good after thousands of tokens: the GPU "100%" at low power, one CPU core
busy, no tokens, no error.

- The pool's workers sleep after 20 ms without work (issue #4). With most
  experts resident many layers have no CPU work, so they also slept
  mid-request, and a worker that woke late was still counted as parked: it
  could claim from the next batch while the host was writing it, run a job
  twice, or add to `done` after the reset - and `done != n` then never
  ended while the GPU waited on the pool. Every claim now carries its
  batch: `head` is one 64-bit word (epoch | njobs | index), a claim is a
  CAS that only succeeds for the epoch the worker woke for, and the host
  waits with `<` instead of `!=`. Same speed (pool_test 47.2 GB/s).
- Every pool wait is bounded (60 s: a message and the engine stops), and
  --serve runs a watchdog: a request with no progress (tokens, prompt
  chunks, verify windows) for STRATA_WATCHDOG_S (120) seconds ends the
  engine with where it was stuck (strata/core/progress.hpp). The server
  (issue #27) answers with an error, names the cause from the log, and
  starts the engine again on the next request.
- pool_stress: tiny batches with sleeping workers; STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US
  shortens the spin to make them sleep constantly.

Tested: pool_test, pool_stress; 25,000-token generation at 262K with KV
streaming and constantly sleeping workers (73.9 tok/s, unchanged); the
watchdog deliberately tripped (2 s): error, log line, restart, next answer.

web app: "Use for other apps too" - the Chat settings as every client's defaults

A switch in the Sampling drawer. With it on, Apply stores the drawer's
settings on the server (POST /settings): thinking level, temperature,
top-p, top-k, seed, max tokens and the experimental speed projection. omp
and other API clients then get them for anything they don't send
themselves, from their next request (no restart); what a client sends still
wins. Off again, clients use their own settings.

- Kept between starts in <config>.shared-settings.json next to the run
  config; the server window says what other apps use.
- Only Strata's own page can change them: JSON only (a cross-site form or
  simple request can't send it without a CORS preflight, which this server
  never grants), no foreign Origin, and the API key when one is set.
- Values are checked (bad ones are a 400 naming the setting).
- Tests: defaults reach the engine, a client's own values win, off clears
  them and the file, 415/403/400/401.
